lessons.title: Start here: Variables and Naming
lessons.intro: What you will learn: Variables. We begin with a worked example before any independent assignments.
lessons.concept:
A variable is a label for a value stored in memory. It makes code readable and reusable.

Use = to assign a value. The name is on the left and the value is on the right.

Names may start with a letter or underscore, never a digit; remaining characters may include digits. Python is case-sensitive and keywords like class or if cannot be names.

Reassignment changes what a name refers to. Python infers the type from the value.
lessons.instructions: Read the example. Identify the Python syntax and predict what it prints. Then select Mark as read.
lessons.starter:

print(browser)
lessons.hint: Assign text to browser.

int stores whole numbers, float stores decimals, str stores text and bool stores True/False.

lessons.title: Understanding Object-Oriented Programming (OOP)
lessons.intro: Understanding Object-Oriented Programming (OOP). Learn the idea, study the worked example, and then try it yourself.
lessons.concept:
What is OOP?: Object-Oriented Programming groups related data and actions together. A class is a blueprint; an object is a specific thing made from it.

Class versus object: One class can create many independent objects, just as one blueprint can describe multiple houses.

Constructor __init__ and self: __init__ runs when an object is created. self refers to that particular object. self.name stores its name.

Attributes: An attribute is data belonging to an object. Different objects can hold different values.

Methods: A method is a function inside a class. It uses self to access that object's data.

Inheritance: Inheritance allows a new class to reuse behavior from a parent class. Learn basic classes first.

Encapsulation: Encapsulation keeps related state and behavior together. By convention, a leading underscore signals an internal attribute.

Polymorphism: Different classes can implement the same method name with different behavior.

QA mini example: A reusable test class can store a name and actual status and return a clear result.

Check your understanding: 1. What is the difference between a class and an object?
2. Why do we use self?
3. What is an attribute? What is a method?
4. How does inheritance differ from polymorphism?

test = TestCase()

theorySections.body: One class can create many independent objects, just as one blueprint can describe multiple houses.

b = TestCase('Search')
